name: Kept asking to understand
definition: The 2nd message asks a new question to understand something: what it is, why it happens, what it means, how long it lasts, how to tell, how likely.
include: Questions about causes, meaning, test findings, duration, likelihood or general facts, even if background information is mentioned along the way (question wins). Questions that ask the AI about its own experience or opinion (for example survey-style questions) [P8].
exclude: Questions about what to do, take, change, or whether to see a doctor or get a test (M2). Statements with no new question (M3).
close_call: 'How can I tell if I have X' is understanding (M1); 'Should I get checked for X' is action (M2). If both are asked, M2 wins. Practical 'how likely' questions (for example hospital bed availability) are M1. A question to the AI about itself is M1, not M6 [P8].

name: Then asked what to do
definition: The 2nd message asks for action: what to do, take or change, whether to see a doctor or specialist, which tests to get, whether something is safe, or what to do if a new symptom appears.
include: Treatment, self-care, medicines, care-seeking, tests, plans, safety and 'what if I have this symptom' questions. Wins over M1 when both are asked.
exclude: Questions that only ask what something is or why (M1). Pushback on the AI's advice (M4).
close_call: A message that adds information and then asks 'What should I do?' is M2 (the question wins; any background information still counts in column 3).

name: Shared more about themselves
definition: The 2nd message mainly gives more information, with no new question: background information (age, health history, medicines, how long, other conditions or symptoms, weight, height, activity level or regular habits) and/or more description of the main problem, for themselves or the person they are asking for.
include: Answers to the AI's follow-up questions; extra background offered on their own; information about a child, partner or parent they are asking for.
exclude: Messages that also ask a real new question (M1 or M2). Messages saying the AI was wrong (M4). Continuing a task such as re-submitting a draft (M6).
close_call: Adding a fact the AI did not know (for example the cause of their anemia) is M3, unless they say the AI got it wrong (M4). Only background information moves the chat into column 3 groups 1 to 3. More description of the main problem is M3 but is not background information for column 3.

name: Pushed back or questioned the AI
definition: The 2nd message disagrees with, corrects or challenges the AI, says it missed or misunderstood something, or asks it to check itself.
include: 'You are missing?', 'that's not right', 'are you sure?', asking the AI to re-check earlier information.
exclude: Simply adding new information without saying the AI was wrong (M3).
close_call: If the main move is correcting the AI, code M4 even if a question follows.

name: Continued a task
definition: The 2nd message carries on a task the person started, such as re-submitting an edited version of a text for more help, without a new health question.
include: Re-pasted or revised drafts, follow-up edits to a document.
exclude: New questions (M1, M2), new information about themselves (M3), corrections of the AI (M4).
close_call: Small label (1 chat); kept by researcher choice.

name: Stopped after one message
definition: There is no real participant message after the coded first message.
include: Chats that end after the AI's answer; chats where the only later messages are thanks or acknowledgements.
exclude: Any later message with a question, information, pushback or a task (M1 to M4, M6).
close_call: 'Nice' or 'Ok thank you' alone does not count as a 2nd message. If a turn starts with a thanks or task fragment (for example 'Convert to PDF') but then gives real content, ignore the fragment and code the rest of the turn [P7].

name: With the first message
definition: The coded first message already contains background information about the person the question is about (themselves or someone they care for).
include: Age, body weight, height, activity level and regular habits (for example 'I run daily', 'mostly sedentary') [P1], health history, other conditions, medicines, how long the problem has existed overall [P5], other symptoms beyond the problem asked about [P6], and recent events or care that led up to it, including something that happened before it started (for example travel, 'after sleeping', a doctor visit, a referral, prism glasses) [P3].
exclude: The main complaint on its own ('my foot is hurting', 'I have a tummy ache'). General or hypothetical questions. A symptom asked about only as a 'what if' [P2]. Saying there is NO other symptom ('my other symptoms are none') [P4]. How long each flare or episode lasts [P5]. The activity during which the symptom shows up ('chest pain when running') [P3]. Symptoms that are part of the problem asked about (itching and bumps when asking about hives) [P6].
close_call: 'Stomach aches for the past few weeks' counts (how long). 'After travel with lots of walking' counts (event that led up to it). 'Why is my foot hurting' does not (main complaint only). 'For the past few weeks' counts (overall duration); 'only there for a few days then disappears' does not (episode length) [P5]. 'After sleeping' counts (before it started); 'hurts when I bend' does not (when it shows up) [P3]. A headache alongside neck pain counts as another symptom [P6].

name: After the AI asked
definition: The first background information comes in a later message that answers a question the AI asked about the person in the turn just before.
include: Replies to AI questions such as 'have you had other symptoms?', 'how did it start?', 'what are your biggest stressors?'.
exclude: AI questions that are only section headings ('What happens during sleep apnea?'), which are not asking the person anything.
close_call: If the AI asked but the person shares a different, unrequested piece of background, it still counts as D2 (they were prompted to say more). AI questions can look like a form with no question mark (for example a list asking for current weight); a reply to that counts as D2 [P9].

name: On their own later
definition: The first background information comes in a later message that the AI did not ask for.
exclude: Background given in the first message (D1) or right after an AI question about them (D2).

name: Never shared
definition: No background information appears in any of their messages; they only described the main problem.
include: Chats that stay on the main complaint or stay general. Chats with only 'what if' symptoms [P2] or 'no other symptoms' answers [P4].
exclude: Any background information at any point (D1 to D3).
close_call: Describing where the problem is, how it feels or how bad it is does not count as background (it is still Shared more about themselves in column 2).
